A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CREME research work. Their main text, equations, figures, table, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison. The original experimental appendix F is retained and reorganized as appendix G in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulations on four optimization problems, including validity–accuracy comparisons, decision-quality results, and sample-size/runtime analyses in Section 4 and appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains original simulation results, revises Figure 3, and adds empirical analyses of loss-bound estimation, conformal correction, and finite-sample error in appendix G.

M1.justification: New appendix F introduces a solver-gap-adjusted estimator that adds known optimization suboptimality gaps to empirical losses before calibration (Equation 13). Algorithm 1 also corrects split-specific indexing, divides averages by the split size rather than total n, and initializes each split's frontier separately. The core estimator and selection/recalibration procedure remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four synthetic task families: linear programming, newsvendor, portfolio selection, and shortest path. The additional analyses do not identify new datasets or task domains. Nonexchangeable data and solver errors are discussed as extensions, without reported evaluations of those scenarios.

E2.justification: Figure 9 adds an uncorrected estimator to a robustness-selection comparison, described as analogous to standard cross-validation tuning. v2 already compared uncorrected Monte Carlo risk estimation, but did not report this selection comparison. The Monte Carlo comparator in Figure 3 and the parametric quantile, empirical quantile, and conformal prediction baselines in Figures 4 and 7 are retained.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes its stated validity calculation to testing empirical expectations, although appendix G.2 retains the earlier formula. The reported shortest-path configuration changes from five paths to three, without establishing whether experiments were rerun. New analyses introduce true-versus-estimated B controls, correction removal, and preference/sample-size sweeps.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained sample-size, grid-size, and preference analyses, v3 adds three substantive checks: sensitivity to replacing the true loss bound with a sample maximum (Figure 8), correction's effect on selected robustness parameters and empirical validity (Figure 9), and empirical error against the theoretical bound (Figure 10). These substantially expand examination of the method's reliability and practical contribution.

E5.justification: v3 newly specifies 100 averaging iterations in Section 4.1 and reports 100 trials with a minimum–maximum error envelope in Figure 10. However, appendix G.2 retains v2's statement of 10 independent replications, so a consistent increase in averaging cannot be established. The existing 20-trial mean ± standard deviation reporting in Table 1 is unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 3 replaces the earlier declining-validity trajectories with trajectories concentrated near full validity under the revised reported calculation; this is not an established same-setting performance gain. New results show sample-bound estimates falling below the reference frontier at n=30, largely similar selections with and without correction but reported empirical validity of 100% versus at most 50%, and empirical MAE below the theoretical bound. Table 1 and Figures 4, 6, and 7 retain their results.

T1.justification: New appendix F defines the solver suboptimality gap and derives validity for the adjusted estimator. Section 3.1 removes its blanket monotonic-loss premise; the original principal theorems and proofs in appendices A–E remain substantively unchanged. v3 also newly calls Equation 6 an upper bound on Equation 5, contradicting the opposite inequality retained in appendix A.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introduction contributions, and central conclusion retain the same claims: inverse conformal risk estimation, distribution-free finite-sample guarantees for miscoverage and regret, certified Pareto frontiers, and support for robustness selection. The added qualifications and extensions do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands applicability and limitations discussion: dependence obstructs the i.i.d. error bound, pruning permits use without majorant consistency, sample-estimated B trades tighter estimates against possible undercoverage, and data splitting sacrifices sample efficiency. The new correction ablation emphasizes reliable risk auditing despite little change in selected parameters. Section 5 also discusses nonexchangeable data, alternative post-selection inference, and solver errors.

D1.justification: The added analyses document sample sizes, correction controls, preference-weight formulas, and error-aggregation details. Algorithm 1's split calculations and the stated shortest-path configuration are corrected. Python, cvxpy/cvxpylayers defaults, existing bound-estimation instructions, and code-access references remain unchanged. Conflicting 100-versus-10 averaging statements limit reproducibility of the revised validity analysis.

R1.justification: v3 adds Berk et al. (2013) on post-selection inference and Tibshirani et al. (2019) on conformal prediction under covariate shift. These support proposed extensions and limitations discussion. The existing related-work account and central novelty positioning remain.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized language corrections, expands and renames the conclusion, adds an affiliation, acknowledgements, and an impact statement, and consolidates experimental appendix subsections under G.2. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 8–10, including bound-comparison panels, correction-ablation panels, and an error plot with a shaded range. Existing display structures largely remain, with appendix figures relocated through reflow. Figure 8 introduces a presentation error: its caption reverses the true-B and sample-B line styles shown in the legend.

improvement.justification: Corrected split calculations and new failure-mode and correction analyses improve transparency. However, v3 leaves its central validity evaluation inconsistently specified: Section 4.1 reports 100-iteration expectations while G.2 retains 10 replications and Figure 6 retains the earlier results. It also introduces an incorrect upper-bound description for Equation 6 and conflicting Figure 8 labels. These problems affect mathematical clarity and interpretation of the new evidence, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
